quiz.title: Quadratic Equations for JEE Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight JEE-level questions on discriminant, nature and location of roots, common roots and inequalities. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: JEE Main and Advanced quadratic equations

questions.q: For what values of k does x² − 4x + k = 0 have real and distinct roots?
questions.explanation: Distinct real roots need discriminant D > 0. Here D = 16 − 4k > 0, so k < 4.

questions.q: If α and β are the roots of 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0, what is α + β?
questions.explanation: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a = 5/2 and the product is c/a = 3/2.

questions.q: The equation x² + px + 12 = 0 has equal roots. What is the value of p (p > 0)?
questions.explanation: Equal roots mean D = 0, so p² = 4·12 = 48, giving p = 4√3 for the positive value.

questions.q: If x² − 3x + 2 = 0 and x² − 5x + 6 = 0 have a common root, that root is:
questions.explanation: Subtract the equations: (−3x + 2) − (−5x + 6) = 2x − 4 = 0, so x = 2, which satisfies both.

questions.q: For all real x, x² + 2x + k > 0. What is the condition on k?
questions.explanation: A quadratic with positive leading coefficient is always positive when D < 0. Here D = 4 − 4k < 0, so k > 1.

questions.q: Both roots of x² − 2mx + (m² − 1) = 0 lie between −2 and 4. This uses which conditions on f(x)?
options: Only that the product of roots is positive
questions.explanation: Location-of-roots for both roots inside (p, q): D ≥ 0, a·f(p) > 0, a·f(q) > 0, and p < −b/2a < q.

questions.q: If α and β are roots of x² − 6x + 4 = 0, what is α² + β²?
The set of values of x satisfying x² − 5x + 6 < 0 is:
questions.explanation: Factor as (x − 2)(x − 3) < 0. An upward parabola is negative between its roots, so 2 < x < 3.

faq.q: What does the discriminant tell you about a quadratic's roots?
faq.a: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant D = b² − 4ac decides everything. D > 0 gives two distinct real roots, D = 0 gives equal (repeated) real roots, and D < 0 gives a pair of complex conjugate roots.

faq.q: How do you find a common root of two quadratic equations?
faq.a: Subtract the two equations to eliminate the x² term; that gives a linear equation whose solution is the common root. Substitute it back to confirm, or use the cross-multiplication condition for both quadratics.

faq.q: What is the condition for a quadratic to be positive for all real x?
faq.a: For ax² + bx + c to be positive for every real x you need a > 0 and D < 0, so the parabola opens upward and never touches the x-axis. If it must be non-negative, allow D ≤ 0.

faq.q: What is the location-of-roots method in JEE quadratics?
faq.a: It places roots relative to a number or interval using the graph of f(x) = ax² + bx + c. You combine the sign of D, the sign of a·f at the boundary points, and the position of the vertex −b/2a to pin down where the roots lie.
